headline: DPWH Pushes Modern Slope-Stabilization Measures for Landslide-Prone Luzon Highways
seoTitle: DPWH Pushes Modern Slope Stabilization for Luzon Highways | FMB News
seoDescription: The DPWH is moving toward more active slope-stabilization measures on landslide-prone mountain roads, including soil nailing and reinforced slope protection.
deck: The public works department is advancing more active slope-protection approaches on landslide-prone mountain corridors, building on techniques already used in earlier Kennon Road rehabilitation projects.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The approved FMB News midday brief reports that the Department of Public Works and Highways is advancing modern slope-stabilization measures for landslide-prone mountain highways in Luzon.

The brief says the approach includes active slope reinforcement such as soil nailing and reinforced drapery systems, with monitoring technology intended to improve early detection of unstable ground conditions. FMB News is attributing those same-day implementation details to the DPWH-sourced newsroom package because the cited August 22 Philippine News Agency article was not independently retrievable in this run.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: DPWH has long used slope trimming, rock netting, retaining structures and soil nailing on Kennon Road and other landslide-prone corridors. Philippine News Agency reporting from earlier rehabilitation work documented soil nailing and other slope-protection structures on critical Kennon Road sections.

The approved brief identifies Kennon Road and Marcos Highway in the Cordilleras, Dalton Pass, and sections of the Olongapo-Bugallon Road as priority corridors for newer protective measures. Those location-specific rollout details remain attributed to the approved brief pending direct retrieval of the same-day DPWH/PNA release.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Mountain road closures can isolate communities, disrupt food and freight movement, and expose motorists and road crews to rockfall and slope-failure hazards. More active stabilization can reduce risk when paired with drainage management, geotechnical assessment, maintenance and credible warning systems.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for DPWH project notices, procurement records and regional engineering updates that identify the exact road sections, budgets, sensor specifications and construction timetables for the new slope-protection works.
